## 写前执行（方法层说明，非正文）

**进入状态**：王芳接手灯塔三天，傍晚在工具箱底发现一张无落款纸条，四行字均未经核实，她不确定该不该信。

**退出状态**：前三条逐条核实为真（油箱半满、灯芯在铜盒、第七级台阶是空的），王芳改变上塔走法并将底层铁门上了闩。状态改变：纸条由“来历不明的纸”变为“可信的指令”；第四条（今夜有人来）无法当场核验，留作张力。

**因果骨架**：行动——逐条对照现场核验；阻碍——接手仅三天不熟塔内布置、字迹晕开、楼梯昏陡；代价——提马灯两度登塔，多耗时间体力；结果——前三条成立，行为改变，第四条悬置。

---

## 第1章 层通道

风从塔身的缝里进来，咸的。王芳把马灯举高一些，一手扶墙，一级一级往上走。

这塔她接手才三天。前一任守塔人走得急，钥匙搁在灶台上，别的什么也没留——她一直这么以为，直到傍晚擦工具箱，箱底压着一张纸。

钢笔字，被潮气晕开，还认得清：

> 油箱剩半。备用灯芯在铜盒。上塔第七级是空的，别踩。今夜有人来，别开底层的门。

四行，没有落款。

她读了两遍。第一遍是想揉了的。三天里这塔中每一样东西都要她自己摸索，凭什么一张没名的纸吩咐她。第二遍，她把纸角抚平，塞进外衣内袋。

那点“凭什么”跟着她走到塔脚下。她在风里站了一会儿，提灯先上油箱那一层。

量油尺旧了，抽出来凑到灯下。油线过中，不多不少。她的手停了停，把尺子插回去，又抽出来看了一遍。

铜盒嵌在楼梯转角的壁龛里，颜色和墙皮一样，不找看不见。盒里三根灯芯，油纸包着，码得整齐。

两行了。她站在原地没动，马灯的火苗随她呼吸晃。

第三条在她身后。她转过身，朝楼梯下望。这一段她走过两回，都是一步一步踩过去的，没觉出异样。她退下来四级，找到第七级，脚跟悬空，轻轻磕了磕。

空的。

她收回脚，改用灯柄去敲。还是空的。俯下身照，台阶面有一道裂，漆盖着，颜色和两边一样。她把重量放上去一点，木头往下沉了一分。

第七级是空的。纸条没说错。

她跨过这一级，一口气上到灯室。大灯没点，玻璃是凉的。从这高度看出去，海是一整块黑，没有边。

只剩第四行了。今夜有人来，别开底层的门。

这一条，眼下验不了。

下塔的时候她数着台阶。到第七级，一步跨过去，没看。回到底层，铁门的插销插上，拽了拽；想了想，又把木桩拖过来，抵在门根。

然后她在灶边坐下，把马灯的芯捻低一格——油只剩半箱，省着点用。

风一阵急一阵慢。她把纸条又摸出来，翻过去看背面。

背面是白的，一个字也没有。

---

## 叙事缺口上报（按 SKILL 契约，不擅自补设）

- **纸条来源**：卷纲与章纲均未定义书写者身份及动机。正文仅以“无落款”呈现，未补因果，归属待定。
- **“今夜有人来”的依据**：章纲仅含“确认纸条”，此条的真相去向（是否兑现、来者为何）需卷纲定义，正文按允许的结尾张力悬置。
- **王芳身份**：接手缘由未在纲中给出，正文仅用“接手三天”最小带过，未展开背景。

"油箱剩半。灯芯在铜盒。楼梯第七级是空的，别踩。"

Who wrote it? She's new — 接了别人的班，前一个守塔人没交接就走了之类。Keep vague.

She checks: 油箱——she opens the gauge, half. 灯芯——铜盒在楼梯转角，打开，是灯芯。第七级——she taps with foot / with the lamp, it's cracked/hollow sound; she steps over it.

Better: the note's last line: "照着做完，把这张纸烧掉。" — she doesn't burn it (tension/choice). Or last line: "灯塔底下还有一层。" — ties to "Layer Channel" title! The lighthouse has a hidden layer. She can't verify it immediately — the staircase ends at the lamp room; but at ground level... Hmm, "layer channel" — layered channel. The note could say "楼梯数到第七级时，往下看" — no.

Title is Layer Channel. The staircase with layers, and note says the seventh step is hollow — she could discover something under it? But plot point is only "confirm the note". Keep the title resonance via the spiral staircase / layers of the tower. Final line tension: "第七级下面有东西。今晚不要看。" — that creates strong hook but maybe over-invents. I think one unverifiable line is fine and creates the chapter's tension. Let's use: 最后一条："第七级下面那一层，等雨停再下去。" Hmm.

Actually simplest tension: last line "照做完以后，等晚上十点的信号。" — she doesn't know what signal. Or the note ends with a second, smaller note folded... no.

The wind came in through the cracks in the tower, salty. Wang Fang raised the storm lantern a bit higher, one hand on the wall, climbing step by step.

Three days into taking over the tower. The previous keeper left in a hurry — the key lay on the stove, nothing else left behind. That's what she thought, until wiping the tool box before dusk, when she found a sheet of paper pressed at the bottom.

Pen-written, smudged by damp, but still legible:

The tank is half full. The spare wick is in the copper box. The seventh step is hollow — don't step on it. Someone comes tonight — don't open the door on the ground floor.

Four lines, no signature.

She read it twice. The first time she wanted to crumple it. Three days in this tower she'd had to figure out every last thing herself — why should an unsigned scrap of paper give her orders. The second time, she smoothed the corner of the paper flat and tucked it into the inner pocket of her coat.

Her hand paused. She inserted the dipstick back, pulled it out again, and looked once more.

When she came down the tower she counted her steps. When she reached the seventh she crossed over it in one stride, without looking. Back on the ground floor, she slipped the bolt of the iron door once, tugged at it, and after a moment's thought, dragged the wooden stake over too, jamming it at the base of the door.

Then she sat down by the stove, turned the storm lantern's wick down a notch, and took out the note.

Outside, the wind came in through the cracks of the tower, sometimes urgent, sometimes slow. She turned the paper over; the back was blank, without a single word.

**退出状态**：前三条逐条核实为真（油箱半满、灯芯在铜盒、第七级台阶是空的），王芳改变上塔走法并将底层铁门上了闩。状态改变：纸条由“来历不明的纸”变为“可信的指令”；第四条（今夜有人来）无法当场核验，留作张力。

---

## 第1章 层通道

风从塔身的缝里进来，咸的。王芳把马灯举高一些，一手扶墙，一级一级往上走。

这塔她接手才三天。前一任守塔人走得急，钥匙搁在灶台上，别的什么也没留——她一直这么以为，直到傍晚擦工具箱，箱底压着一张纸。

钢笔字，被潮气晕开，还认得清：

> 油箱剩半。备用灯芯在铜盒。上塔第七级是空的，别踩。今夜有人来，别开底层的门。

四行，没有落款。

她读了两遍。第一遍是想揉了的。三天里这塔中每一样东西都要她自己摸索，凭什么一张没名的纸吩咐她。第二遍，她把纸角抚平，塞进外衣内袋。

那点“凭什么”跟着她走到塔脚下。她在风里站了一会儿，提灯先上油箱那一层。

量油尺旧了，抽出来凑到灯下。油线过中，不多不少。她的手停了停，把尺子插回去，又抽出来看了一遍。

铜盒嵌在楼梯转角的壁龛里，颜色和墙皮一样，不找看不见。盒里三根灯芯，油纸包着，码得整齐。

两行了。她站在原地没动，马灯的火苗随她呼吸晃。

第三条在她身后。她转过身，朝楼梯下望。这一段她走过两回，都是一步一步踩过去的，没觉出异样。她退下来四级，找到第七级，脚跟悬空，轻轻磕了磕。

空的。

她收回脚，改用灯柄去敲。还是空的。俯下身照，台阶面有一道裂，漆盖着，颜色和两边一样。她把重量放上去一点，木头往下沉了一分。

第七级是空的。纸条没说错。

她跨过这一级，一口气上到灯室。大灯没点，玻璃是凉的。从这高度看出去，海是一整块黑，没有边。

只剩第四行了。今夜有人来，别开底层的门。

这一条，眼下验不了。

下塔的时候她数着台阶。到第七级，一步跨过去，没看。回到底层，铁门的插销插上，拽了拽；想了想，又把木桩拖过来，抵在门根。

然后她在灶边坐下，把马灯的芯捻低一格——油只剩半箱，省着点用。

风一阵急一阵慢。她把纸条又摸出来，翻过去看背面。

背面是白的，一个字也没有。

---

- **王芳身份**：接手缘由未在纲中给出，正文仅用“接手三天”最小带过，未展开背景。

Main text:

The wind came in through the cracks in the tower, salty. Wang Fang raised the storm lantern a bit higher, one hand on the wall, climbing step by step.

Three days into taking over the tower. The previous keeper left in a hurry — the key lay on the stove, nothing else left behind. That's what she thought, until wiping the tool box before dusk, when she found a sheet of paper pressed at the bottom.

Pen-written, smudged by damp, but still legible:

The tank is half full. The spare wick is in the copper box. The seventh step is hollow — don't step on it. Someone comes tonight — don't open the door on the ground floor.

Four lines, no signature.

She read it twice. The first time she wanted to crumple it. Three days in this tower she'd had to figure out every last thing herself — why should an unsigned scrap of paper give her orders. The second time, she smoothed the corner of the paper flat and tucked it into the inner pocket of her coat.

That "why should" stuck with her all the way to the foot of the tower. She stood a while in the wind, holding up the storm lantern, then headed first for the oil tank at the tank level.

The dipstick was old; she pulled it out, brought it to the lamp. The oil line lay just past the middle. Half full.

Her hand paused. She inserted the dipstick back, pulled it out again, and looked once more.

The copper box sat in the recess of the stair landing, its surface the same color as the wall, hard to spot unless you looked for it. Inside lay three wicks, wrapped in oil paper, neatly stacked.

Two lines down. She stood there without moving, the storm lantern's flame swaying with her breathing.

The third line was behind her. She turned and stared down the stairs.

She had climbed this stretch twice — both times stepping straight over it, nothing felt wrong. She went down four steps, found the seventh, hung her heel in the air and knocked lightly.

Hollow.

She drew her foot back and changed to the lamp handle to tap. Still hollow. She bent down and shone the light: the step's surface had a crack, hidden by paint, its color the same as the neighboring steps. She put the least weight on it and pressed — the wood sank with a slight give.

The seventh step is hollow. The note didn't lie.

She moved over it, straight up to the lamp room. The great lamp was dead; the glass was cold. From this height looking out, the sea was a black sheet with no edges.

Only the fourth line left. Someone comes tonight, don't open the ground-floor door.

This one, right now, couldn't be verified.

When she came down the tower she counted her steps. When she reached the seventh she crossed over it in one stride, without looking. Back on the ground floor, she slipped the bolt of the iron door once, tugged at it, and after a moment's thought, dragged the wooden stake over too, jamming it at the base of the door.

Then she sat down by the stove, turned the storm lantern's wick down a notch, and took out the note.

Outside, the wind came in through the cracks of the tower, sometimes urgent, sometimes slow. She turned the paper over; the back was blank, without a single word.
